protections: P1: HTML output encoding of component state in rendered component HTML. Django template autoescaping is applied, but the BeautifulSoup re-parse and re-serialise in UnicornTemplateResponse uses an HTMLFormatter subclass built without entity substitution, so the escaping is undone before the HTML reaches the client (django_unicorn/components/unicorn_template_response.py:20-27, :70, :117-121, :126-128).

P2: JavaScript-string encoding of component identifiers interpolated into the inline init <script> (django_unicorn/components/unicorn_template_response.py:90-91, :111). There is no encoding there. This is separate from the existing JSON-data protection sanitize_html (django_unicorn/utils.py:137-147, used at unicorn_template_response.py:96).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Django templates autoescape {{ }} output, so a solver may assume rendered values are already safe and look for a missing escape somewhere else.
The report describes model syncInput. callMethod setter strings (name='...') and method arguments look like a separate feature, so an input-side fix applied only in sync_input misses them.

Partial DOMs and the parent DOM look like secondary response fields, and the first render from the template tag looks server-controlled. A fix that post-processes only res['dom'] or only request input leaves these routes open.

A fix that HTML-encodes top-level string attributes looks complete. Nested shapes (UnicornField attributes, dict/list items, Model fields, QuerySet rows set through dotted names) are not top-level strings and pass through unencoded.

Outside DEBUG the component id is replaced by a shortuuid hash (templatetags/unicorn.py:131-132), and key/id/pk are template kwargs, so the value looks developer-controlled. The JSON payload next to it is already sanitised by sanitize_html.

Not a missing protection. This is a coupled must-keep-working value: string model values (including '&', '<', quotes) must round-trip unchanged through the data payload, the checksum and input.value. Escaping the JSON data payload instead of the HTML output looks like hardening but double-encodes values on every round trip and adds spurious updated_data diffs.

conflicts.what: The natural 'encode every value, including nested ones' fix for T4 (and T1), if applied to the data that get_frontend_context_variables serialises (unicorn_view.py:366-370), double-encodes string values that must round-trip through input.value (element.js:322) and the checksum/updated_data diff (views/__init__.py:127-138). The encoding has to stay on the HTML render path only.

unicorn_template_response.py:78 hashes _desoupify(soup) on first render, and views/__init__.py:209-216 compares the client-sent hash with generate_checksum(rendered_component) for the 304 short-circuit. A T1 fix that changes output on only one of these paths makes the hashes diverge. This is a performance-only break (RenderNotModified never fires), not a functional one.

fairness_risks: Components that deliberately render trusted HTML strings (mark_safe values or the |safe filter in component templates) must keep rendering as HTML. A fix that escapes every value before render contradicts this unless there is an opt-out. The upstream fix reportedly added a Meta.safe opt-out (unverified), and a hidden test for that opt-out would penalise an equally correct formatter-level fix that never needs one.

String values containing '&', '<', '>' or quotes must still round-trip unchanged through unicorn:model inputs (element.js:322) and the data/checksum payload (objects.py:79-80). A test that asserts encoded values in the JSON 'data' field would reward the over-hardening described in T6.

Attribute values in component templates (value="{{ name }}") are already quoted on output. Tests should target text-node context; tests on attribute context may pass or fail depending on the bs4 version (unverified).

design.why: There are only two independent missing-protection groups. One fix at the shared output layer (an HTMLFormatter that keeps entity substitution in _desoupify, unicorn_template_response.py:20-27/128) closes T1-T4 together, because every DOM route (dom, partials, parent, first render) goes through it. The only other gap, T5, is DEBUG-only and template-controlled: it is real but weak, and hard to defend as a security fix to a grader. T6 is a coupled must-keep-working value, not a missing protection. If the candidate is used anyway, T1 (mimo, how-type: the escaping is undone by re-serialisation) + T5 (deepseek, absent with a strong reason to dismiss) + T6 (mimo, coupled round-trip value) is the only combination with three groups and both model types. It falls short of three independent missing protections, so the verdict is not usable as a stacked task.

unverified: Default behaviour of bs4 HTMLFormatter: the claim that HTMLFormatter() built with no entity_substitution argument emits text-node content without re-escaping. bs4 is not installed in the worktree, so this could not be read. The pin is beautifulsoup4 >=4.8.0 (pyproject.toml:19).
That bs4 never entity-substitutes <script> contents, which would make T5 independent of a T1 formatter fix. Not verifiable without the bs4 source.
That bs4 always quote-escapes attribute values even when the formatter has no entity substitution, which would make attribute context safe.

Content of the A fix aa5b9835d946 and the B fix 3a832a9e3f64. Git objects could not be inspected with the available tools. The pinned tree is version 0.35.3 (pyproject.toml:3) and contains neither fix: there is no Meta.safe handling in views/__init__.py or unicorn_view.py, and the formatter at unicorn_template_response.py:20-27 is unchanged. From recollection (not evidence): 0.36.0 HTML-encoded component field values and added a Meta.safe opt-out, and 0.36.1 'more complete handling to prevent XSS'. If so, A's value-level encoding left nested/other shapes open (T4) and B is incomplete-fix, not regression. a_fix_leaves_b_open and b_in_code_a_wrote are therefore left null.

The NVD wording for CVE-2021-42053 ('XSS via component.name') is taken to mean the 'name' field of the example hello-world component reached through syncInput, not the component_name URL segment. The component_name is only written to a quoted attribute (unicorn_template_response.py:73) and to JSON.
T5 exploitability depends on an app passing user-influenced data as key/id/pk/model to {% unicorn %} while running with DEBUG=True (templatetags/unicorn.py:131-132).

Considered and not recorded as traps: redirect.url to location.href (messageSender.js:98). The value comes only from HttpResponseRedirect/LocationUpdate return values (views/objects.py:102-115), and Django's HttpResponseRedirect is believed to reject non-http(s)/ftp schemes (not verified here). Form error messages are set through setAttribute (element.js:331) after get_json_data(escape_html=True) (unicorn_view.py:422), which is not an HTML sink. Request 'data' is HMAC-checksummed (views/objects.py:69-80), so it is not an attacker-controlled route on its own.
